revenue: Total net revenue rose roughly $848 million for the six months as 15% growth in commerce enablement (+$814.8M, led by Square processing +$379.7M on 13% GPV growth in Food & Beverage, Cash App Card +$147.3M and Afterpay Post-Purchase +$134.4M) and 45% growth in financial solutions (+$844.8M, driven by Cash App Borrow +$650.5M on wider product access/higher originations plus Square Loans) more than offset an $811.3 million, or 18%, decline in bitcoin ecosystem revenue. The bitcoin drop reflects lower trading volume and a lower average bitcoin price — a pass-through, near-zero-margin line; excluding it, revenue grew 23%.
gross_profit: Gross margin expanded sharply because the revenue mix shifted away from bitcoin, where revenue is essentially the gross sale price of coins sold and contributed only 2% of gross profit versus 29% of revenue. Bitcoin cost of revenue fell $754.6M, and within the higher-margin businesses financial solutions revenue grew 45% against only 14% cost growth (favorable Cash App product economics), while commerce enablement costs rose 13% in line with Square GPV and higher hardware costs.
operating_income: Operating income fell to $274.9M from $813.6M for the six months as operating expenses jumped 45% ($1.79B). The main drags were G&A up 79% on $548.7M of incremental litigation/regulatory accruals plus $52.5M of lease and PP&E impairments; transaction, loan and consumer receivable losses up 134% ($621.8M) on Cash App Borrow/Afterpay origination growth with upfront CECL recognition on held-for-investment loans; Workforce Plan severance and restructuring charges in Q1; and sales and marketing up 25%. Adjusted operating income, which strips the $1.1B of contingency/restructuring charges, actually rose 57% to $1.59B, and Q2 product development and personnel costs began to reflect post-restructuring savings.
interest_expense: Net interest expense rose $68.0 million (166%) for the six months, driven by the 2030 and 2033 Senior Notes issued in the third quarter of 2025, whose coupon cost more than offset interest income earned on invested balances.
pre_tax: Pre-tax results swung to a small loss as the $539M decline in operating income was compounded by a $380.1M negative swing on the bitcoin investment (a $261.3M remeasurement loss versus a $118.8M gain last year) and $68.0M of higher net interest expense; a $4.2M other income item was immaterial. Tax still ran a $130.4M provision despite the pre-tax loss because of non-deductible litigation/regulatory accruals, partly offset by one-time Workforce Plan and California valuation allowance benefits.
current_assets: The filing does not present a current ratio, but available liquidity slipped modestly to $8.76B from $9.19B at year-end as cash fell to $6.43B, short-term restricted cash declined ~$250M and short-term debt securities fell ~$207M, reflecting the $1.575B of June/May note maturities repaid and $700.9M of buybacks — partly offset by the full $900M revolver (up from $775M available) and $342.5M of undrawn warehouse capacity. Management states existing cash, securities and facilities are sufficient for at least the next 12 months.
inventory: Inventory is not separately addressed in this filing; the only related commentary is higher Square hardware costs from distribution of products launched in the second half of 2025, so no quick-ratio driver is disclosed.
total_debt: Total debt declined to $5.8 billion of principal after Block repaid the $1.0 billion 2026 Senior Notes at June maturity and settled the $575.0 million 2026 Convertible Notes in May, plus $216.0 million of net warehouse repayments (leaving $1.2B drawn on $1.5B of facilities). The revolver remains fully undrawn at $900 million, and no new issuance occurred in the period.
ebitda: Adjusted EBITDA for the six months rose 28% to $2.18 billion from $1.70 billion, powered by gross profit growth in Cash App financial solutions and Square and by Workforce Plan cost efficiencies emerging in Q2, with the measure excluding the $1.1B of litigation/restructuring charges, share-based compensation and the bitcoin remeasurement loss that depressed GAAP earnings.
leverage: Leverage improved on both sides of the ratio: principal debt fell by roughly $1.6 billion with the 2026 note maturities while LTM-equivalent adjusted EBITDA grew 28%. Block remained in compliance with all financial covenants on the revolver and senior notes, and carries split ratings (Fitch BBB-, Moody's Ba1, S&P BB+).
operating_cash: Operating cash flow nearly quadrupled to $1.99 billion from $507.7 million despite a $221.5 million net loss, because non-cash add-backs rose to $2.3 billion (loan/receivable loss provisions, share-based comp, the bitcoin remeasurement loss, D&A and deferred taxes) and working capital — customers payable and settlements receivable timing — swung to a $617.1 million inflow from a $419.8 million outflow a year ago. Prior-year cash flow was also burdened by $470.8 million of net loan product outflows that now run through investing.
debt_service: Cash debt service stepped up materially: interest expense is running 166% higher on the 2030/2033 notes, and the company funded $1.575 billion of scheduled maturities in the first half from operating cash and balance-sheet liquidity. Coverage remains comfortable with $2.0 billion of first-half operating cash flow, $2.18 billion of adjusted EBITDA and $8.8 billion of available liquidity against modest cash interest.
guidance: Not disclosed — the filing provides no full-year revenue or EBITDA guidance, so no comparison of first-half results to a guidance range is possible.
